narr: A stationary front draped north of West Viginia led to several rounds of showers and storms between July 5th and 6th. Overnight clusters of activity diminished each morning, allowing for a brief window of reprieve. This allowed the atmosphere to recharge for renewed convection during the afternoon and evening time frame. These storms contributed to downed trees from damaging wind gusts and localized instances of flash flooding due to heavy downpours. Over an inch of rain fell within strong and mature storms on these two days.
